title: Indonesia Nickel Processing
thesis: Snowflake turns daily line data from a synthetic network of Indonesian nickel processing lines (RKEF and HPAL) into nickel-recovery KPIs, 7-day upset-risk scores, setpoint deviation anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Nickel recovery, process upsets, energy intensity and ore processed for 24 lines across 5 Indonesian sites.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to line-day rows.
The nickel-lost chart shows which upset causes cost the most contained nickel.
show: Nickel not recovered by root cause
tabs.call_out: One governed set of processing KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which lines are likely to have the next upset?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each line's probability of a process upset in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags setpoint deviation outliers per line, and the forecast projects network-wide nickel recovery for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the lines behind those risks?

talking_points: Line availability and critical spares coverage frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against nickel recovery by line shows where discipline and recovery move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, upset, cause and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a line alarms right now?

talking_points: Live line readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the line's current risk band, then emails the process metallurgist.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
